to.name: Ba’ale Wold / Feast of God the Son

evidence.text: Praising God the Son Incarnate for our salvation
Monthly commemoration of the Annunciation of the Lord (Bisrate Gabriel, 29th of month)
Uriel is addressed and praised throughout every stanza; intercession and healing are attributed to him.
መስቀል ብርሃነ ለኩሉ ዓለም መሠረተ ቤተክርስቲያን
Both the Ge’ez opening and Amharic restatement repeatedly name the Cross as the hymn's subject.
Most stanzas celebrate God's mercy and urge praise. Mary appears near the close as intercessor, not the main addressee.
The refrain calls for praise of God; the sea and Jericho are separate examples of divine power. Trinity and Mary are incidental mentions.
Michael is invoked line after line for intercession, protection, and rescue; the Bahran story supports the same focus.
The repeated direct petition asks God to protect Ethiopia and its defenders and grant peace; it is not a named feast or saint hymn.
The Ge’ez opening and repeated Amharic response center Michael's rescue of Bahran; Moses is an additional illustration.
After narrating Christ's suffering, the singer repeatedly examines hollow worship and asks to obey in love. The moral appeal is the dominant purpose.
The song opens by praising God and narrates Moses at the sea, but its repeated interpretive refrain names Michael as Israel's guide. Editorial review should confirm the intended balance.
The Ge’ez appeal and Amharic stanzas ask Uriel for intercession and help; God is the recipient of the prayer Uriel carries.
የአምላክ ስም አለበት ስሙ ሚካኤል ነው
Multiple stanzas recount Michael's protection and upbringing of the singer; other biblical references are figurative background.
Separate stanzas recount Bartimaeus, the woman with bleeding, and the sick man at the pool as examples of God's healing and saving action.
